s1.subtitle: Art & Technology: Artistic Theory and Practice in the AI Era
s1.title_main: Translating Heritage Vocabulary via Generative AI
s1.title_sub: ——Knitwear Design Inspired by Jiangxi Xiabu Embroidery
s1.author: School of Fashion Design | Yunkyung Lee
s1.event: Academic Forum - Nanchang Key Laboratory of AI Manufacturing
s1.quote: “My focus lies in Jiangxi Xiabu Embroidery. My objective is not simply ‘transplanting it onto garments’, but rather taking its true essence—the base fabric, linear rhythm, and negative spatial relations—and rewriting them into modern knit parameters.”

s2.p2_sub: 01. Problem Statement: Why Surface Borrowing Always Fails
s2.p2_t1: Let me begin by addressing a very fundamental question: Why can't we simply borrow patterns? Patterns are the easiest elements to extract and replicate. Yet, when only surface patterns remain, the profound foundational logic defining the tradition inevitably vanishes.
s2.p2_t2: We compartmentalize this into three distinct tiers: (1) Pattern Copying, (2) Material Logic Translation, and (3) Cultural Semantic Preservation. By consequence, we must pose a deeper inquiry than 'Does it look similar?' We must ask: 'Why does it manifest this way, and can this structural logic be assimilated into contemporary knitting parameters?'
s2.p2_t3: We are pivoting away from superficial pattern comparison. Instead, we scrutinize how the base fabric, threads, and negative spaces of Xiabu Embroidery correspond to the mesh, linear organization, and openwork structures of knitted textiles.
s2.p2_quote: “This is not pattern replication; it is a translation of structural logic.”
s2.p3_sub: 02. Literature Review: Unbridged Gaps at the Intersection
s2.p3_t1: Current research predominantly explores three avenues: First, enhancing the visual realism of generated garment imagery; Second, pivoting toward material simulation and physical physics; Third, digitizing heritage resources for knowledge representation.
s2.p3_t2: While all three streams are crucial, the critical flaw is their lack of organic integration. Visual generation researchers seldom process material verification. Physics simulation teams typically overlook cultural semantics. Heritage digitization often stagnates at mere classification.
s2.p3_path1_sub: From Style Generation to Physical Credibility
s2.p3_path1_li1: Choi et al. (2023): AI-assisted fashion design systems focusing on visual style formulation
s2.p3_path1_li2: Drape (2023): Inferring fabric mechanics from depth maps with physical parameters
s2.p3_path1_li3: D-Garment (2025): Physically-conditioned latent diffusion for simulation-ready outputs
s2.p3_path1_li4: DiffusedWrinkles (2025): High-fidelity wrinkle diffusion for drape authenticity
s2.p3_path2_li1: Drape (2023): Depth map → Fabric mechanic estimation (Pioneering work)
s2.p3_path2_li2: Inverse Garment (2024): Differential simulation to trace back patterns and materials
s2.p3_path2_li3: D-Garment (2025): Learning material-physics topologies in latent space
s2.p3_path3_sub: From Archival Recording to Knowledge Structuring
s2.p3_path3_li1: Heritage Review (2024): A systematic review of 3D reconstruction pipelines
s2.p3_path3_li2: Wu & Li (2024): Initial explorations of Generative AI for knit topologies
s2.p3_path3_li3: Knowledge Graph (2025): Semantic representation algorithms for costume matching
s2.p3_t3: Consequently, my research is positioned securely at this intersection. My concern is: How can we translate the cultural semantics and material characteristics of heritage into verifiable, functional parametric languages ready for digital sample validation? Simply stated:
s2.p3_quote: “Empowering AI to transcend mere image drawing by equipping it with material comprehension.”
s2.p4_box1_li1: 1. Operability Gap (Lack of Verification): Outputs must exceed ocular similarity and directly interface with digital pattern/structural validation.
s2.p4_box1_li2: 2. Methodological Gap (Translation Mechanisms): How exactly do traditional traits like transparency, thread rhythms, and negative space mathematically map onto stitch gauge, yarn, topology, and density?
s2.p4_box1_li3: 3. Cultural Gap (Semantic Loss): Does the end product reflect the true cultural ideology, or is it merely reduced to an algorithmic surface pattern?
s2.p4_box2_desc: My proposition is not a monolithic point solution, but rather a unified methodology encompassing three simultaneous frameworks:
s2.p4_box2_quote: “By binding these frameworks, I seek to permanently interlock the original problem, the methodology, and the evaluative criteria into an inextricably linked system.”

s3.p5_sub: 04. Conceptual Framework: Tracing the Three Layers
s3.p5_t1: The core conceptual pillar of this research relies on fracturing the translation mechanism into three distinct layers:
s3.p5_layer1_desc: Pertains strictly to interpreting the ontological meaning of the heritage craft—e.g., Xiabu Embroidery's translucent base, rhythmic linearity, and aesthetics of emptiness.
s3.p5_layer2_desc: By bypassing literal patterns, semantics are extracted into intermediate structural logic: Transparency, Rhythmic Motion, Negative Shape.
s3.p5_layer3_desc: The final stage where logic solidifies into tangible, mathematically controllable gauges, yarn types, topological meshes, and density.
s3.p5_t2: Summarily, the tiers mandate three subsequent actions: Semantic Comprehension → Abstract Logic Extraction → Industrial Implementation.
s3.p5_quote: “The middle phase constitutes the absolute crux. The pervasive failing within modern digitizations is directly leaping from cultural significance to visual modeling. I aim to construct the missing operative bridge.”
s3.p6_t1: Beyond conceptual theories, practical application necessitates an actionable pipeline. I present a closed-loop human-in-the-loop (HITL) methodology.
s3.p6_t2: Within this epistemology, AI does not serve as an autonomous surrogate for designers; it functions strictly as an accelerative catalyst.
s3.p6_t3: LLMs synthesize semantics; Generative diffusion networks widen design probabilities; CLO 3D forces these possibilities through structural simulation bottlenecks. The absolute authority over aesthetic filtering and cultural fidelity permanently resides with the human.
s3.p6_quote: The priority is not generative acceleration, but verification. Every stage must be retrospectable, amendable, and decipherable. This dictates my unyielding emphasis on the 'Closed Loop' principle.

s4.p7_t1: The flanking subsidiary studies (Weave and Suture) are not merely parallel artifacts. The primary case (Sheer) proves the fundamental validity of the hypothesis on the core subject, while the secondary cases substantiate the model's scalability and structural migration capabilities to disparate textile systems.
s4.p7_t2: Visually manifesting as diverse languages, they fundamentally act as three empirically distinct translation trajectories.
s4.p7_case1_desc: Isolating translucent substrates, linear rhythms, and semantic voids.
s4.p7_case2_desc: Codifying lattice-memory, pixel taxonomy, and density flux gradients.
s4.p7_case3_desc: Addressing hairline tactility, reparative semantics, and structural perimeters.
s4.p8_t1: The resolved garment imagery presented here constitutes a byproduct; what legitimizes it is an exhaustive chain of translational rationale.
s4.p8_t2:
Stage 1 (Source Image): Identifying original translucent ramie substrates alongside linear threading logic.
Stage 2 (Logic Distillation): Condensing the craft into core algorithms: Transparency, Vector Rhythm, and Negative Fill.
Stage 3 (Parametric Swatches): Corresponding aforementioned variables to Mesh topographies, Linear stitch organizations, and Openwork configurations.
Stage 4 (CLO 3D Verification): Elevating the artifact from a 'shallow render' into a physically verifiable manufacturing state.
s4.p8_quote: “The objective was never to produce a garment simulating the 'look' of Xiabu craft. Core intention: Reassembling translucent topology, skeletal framework, and void relations into native knitting vocabularies. The supremacy of the main case lies not in its silhouette, but its unwavering evidentiary chain.”
s4.p9_t1: The source material reflects the orthodox orthogonal lattice configurations indigenous to Wanzai ramie weaving. The priority resides not in mimicking a mundane generic plaid aesthetic, but probing whether orthographic repetitive orders can be legitimately rewritten into programmatic knit pixel logic.
s4.p9_t2: To execute this, three protocols are engaged: Sampling (extracting base intersection units); Quantization (transfiguring the organic weave into quantized pixel blocks and grayscale gradations); Mapping (integrating parameters via 5-7gg intarsia alongside rigorous localized mesh density manipulations).
s4.p9_t3: The resultant artifact proves that lattice-memory does not perish upon computational transformation; it metamorphoses into an advanced parametric arrangement dictating structural and visual density fluctuations.
s4.p9_quote: Transitioning from weaving to knitting is not an act of visual appropriation; it mandates a holistic conversion of the tectonic architecture.
s4.p10_t1: Case 3 examines Ganfa embroidery—notorious for employing human hair as thread—and theorizes how its excruciatingly fine and restrained tracking philosophies evolve into overt contemporary structural sutures.
s4.p10_t2:
Stage 1 (Heritage Baseline): Observing unparalleled, intensely directional microscopic thread paths utilizing human hair.
Stage 2 (Abstract Mapping): Abandoning literal biomaterial replication (hair), the model isolates the psychological semantics of the lines: repairing, binding, and bordering. Resulting vectors: Suturing Semantic, Stitch Pathing, Structural Boundary.
Stage 3 (Implementation): Realized via industrial 12gg jacquard, aggressive contrast coloration, and micro-suturing textures.
s4.p10_t3: The final technical blueprint is presented not to flaunt gratuitous complexity, but to substantiate that esoteric metaphysical cultural cues can—and must—climax into actionable structural outcomes.
s4.p10_quote: Authentic paradigm translation rarely preserves identical morphologies. It demands the radical rewriting of underlying structural dependencies.

s5.p11_t1: Charting the three case studies against five rigorous evaluative vectors produces the matrix. The assessment encompasses five non-trivial pillars: fidelity of cultural resonance, macroscopic material cohesion, physical reliability in drape mechanics, deterministic structural logic, and intensive qualitative expert review.
s5.p11_t2: The ubiquitous failure across contemporary AI fashion discourse is the over-saturation of hyper-aestheticized renders lacking any critical, quantifiable, and recursive evaluative methodology.
s5.p11_t3: Consequently, the gravity of this matrix is not derived from boasting iteration volume. Its sole purpose is to declare:
s5.p11_quote1: “These generational outputs are actively judged, contrasted, and systematically corrected.”
s5.p11_dim1_desc: Assessing whether parametric interventions retained the original heritage narrative logic.
s5.p11_dim2_desc: Evaluating fidelity between virtual digital substrates against physical reference variables.
s5.p11_dim3_desc: Validating gravitation estimations surrounding generated fabric behavior models.
s5.p11_dim4_desc: Ensuring structural openworks, mesh typologies, and loops align with manufacturing integrities.
s5.p11_dim5_desc: Deploying qualitative oversight algorithms via heritage sector professionals.
s5.p11_ai_desc: Reflecting on the matrix necessitates delineating algorithmic functionality from human directive logic:
s5.p11_ai_role1_desc: Optimized to unlock dimensionality. Computes enormous variants of structural mutations at high velocity.
s5.p11_ai_role2_desc: Optimized for directional consensus. Governs the ultimate qualitative, cultural, and aesthetic resolutions.
s5.p11_ai_quote:
“AI is categorically not supplanting the designer. In unequivocally clear terms:
AI obliterates boundaries; Human intuition stabilizes the trajectory.”

s6.p12_t1: Summarizing the empirical advancements yielded by this study highlights three cornerstone milestones:
s6.p12_card1_desc: Engineered the Tri-Layered Translation Model bridging intangible Semantic Concepts to intermediate Material Logic, finalized as concrete Parametric Math.
s6.p12_card2_desc: Standardized a heavily fragmented toolset (LLM, T2I, 3D modeling, Human Review) into a singular, highly robust Closed-Loop generative pipeline.
s6.p12_card3_desc: Verified the hypothesis that this structure serves as a supremely adaptable training methodology targeting next-generation digital fashion curation integration.
s6.p12_limit_desc: Admittedly, this investigation possesses explicit finite operational boundaries. Current validations address a restricted taxonomy of textiles. Furthermore, reliance predominantly on pure virtual 'Simulation-Ready' strata dictates an urgent requirement to synthesize physical knit testing and aggressive friction experiments in sequential iterations.
s6.p12_quote:
“To conclude this discourse, I reiterate the absolute baseline truth:
The ultimate existential threat facing heritage crafts is not invisibility. It is the tragic reductionism into trivial, decorative surface textures.
My unwavering objective is forcing craft logic, material wisdom, and heritage semantics to dynamically evolve and assert themselves within dominant contemporary infrastructures.”
s6.p13_t1: The bibliographical architecture underpinning this protocol fundamentally relies on three disparate vectors of contemporary research:
s6.p13_ref1_1: D-Garment (2025): Physics-conditioned latent diffusion frameworks validating functional generation.
s6.p13_ref1_2: DiffusedWrinkles (2025): Algorithms engineered exclusively for high-fidelity localized textile drape distortion.
s6.p13_ref1_3: Inverse Garment Pattern (2024): Machine learning inverse parameter estimation models via differentiable topologies.
s6.p13_ref1_4: How Will It Drape (2023): Utilizing depth map data to calculate macro fabric mass and tensor strain values.
s6.p13_ref2_1: An & Park (2026): Widespread adoption impact metrics associated with systemic AI educational tool integrations.
s6.p13_ref2_2: Wu & Li (2024): AIGC deployments aimed distinctly at jacquard and knit topological variations.
s6.p13_ref2_3: Choi et al. (2023): Feasibility documentation targeting total automation workflows within mass textile design centers.
s6.p13_ref3_1: Knowledge Graph (2025): Compendium building via complex semantic node matching algorithms against archival costume databases.
s6.p13_ref3_2: Heritage Review (2024): Aggregate evaluation regarding 3D point-cloud mapping efficiency against traditional analogue restoration practices.
s6.p13_desc:
Isolating these literature clusters is inconsequential. However, strategically weaponizing them in synergy proves unequivocally that:

Heritage preservation frameworks, cutting-edge generational models, and industrial machine knitting logic can—and must—intersect across unified macroscopic ecosystems.
s6.p13_end: This concludes my presentation. I welcome any inquiries, critiques, or analytical discourse at this time.
s6.p13_summary_title: Three Replicable Mantras Underlying this Research
s6.p13_summary_1: Not an imitation of surfaces, but a translation of systems.
s6.p13_summary_2: Not optimizing visual allure, but mandating computational verifiability.
s6.p13_summary_3: Not allowing heritage to calcify in history, but ensuring it achieves contemporary survival.
